sample_modal.title: Here's what you'll see at the end
sample_modal.body: Not just a guide — a synthesised read of what 25 participants told you, grouped into themes with verbatims you can quote in a deck. Drafted from a 2-minute conversation.

example.name: Why new signups never run their first interview
example.objective: Understand what stops trial users from launching their first study so we know which onboarding friction to fix first.
example.q1_question: Walk me through what you were trying to do the first time you logged in.
example.q2_question: Was there a moment you thought "this isn't for me right now"? Tell me about it.
example.q3_question: If you could have skipped one step, which one would it have been?

themes.title: "I didn't know who I'd interview"
themes.finding: 12 of 25 stalled before launching because they hadn't lined up participants. They expected the tool to find people for them.
themes.quote: I assumed there'd be a panel I could just send it to. When I realised I had to bring my own list, I closed the tab.
themes.speaker: Maya, PM at a 40-person SaaS

themes.title: The first study felt high-stakes
themes.finding: Trial users described the first study as "my one shot." They over-edited the question guide and never sent it.
themes.quote: I rewrote those five questions seven times. I was sure I was going to waste my participants' time.
themes.speaker: Jonas, founder, B2B fintech

themes.title: Voice felt risky without seeing the output
themes.finding: Users who didn't see a sample transcript before launching were 3x more likely to abandon. The AI felt opaque.
themes.quote: I didn't know what the AI would actually do once people started talking. I needed to see one finished interview before trusting it.
themes.speaker: Lina, UX researcher at a marketplace

example.name: Why architects pick one specification database over another
example.objective: Understand the moment architects choose which product database to trust for a project, so we know which credibility signals matter most.
example.q1_question: Walk me through the last project where you had to specify a product you hadn't used before. What was the trigger?
example.q2_question: What made you trust one source over another when comparing options? Tell me about a specific moment.
example.q3_question: When have you walked away from a product you'd otherwise have specified? Why?

themes.title: Reference projects beat brochures every time
themes.finding: 18 of 25 architects said a built example near their site weighed more than any technical sheet — but only 2 said brands made finding one easy.
themes.quote: If I can't find a project like mine where it's already been installed, I move on. I'm not the first person to test it on a client.
themes.speaker: Anne, architect, mid-sized firm

themes.title: BIM-ready or it doesn't get specified
themes.finding: If the BIM object wasn't downloadable in under a minute, the product dropped out of the shortlist. Brand recognition didn't save it.
themes.quote: I'm not going to model it myself. If their Revit file isn't there, I pick the competitor whose file is.
themes.speaker: Marc, BIM coordinator, design-build firm

themes.title: The client's compliance officer has veto power
themes.finding: Architects pre-filter for certifications because the legal/compliance team will kill the spec late if missing. They route around products that look risky.
themes.quote: I learned the hard way — picked the better product, compliance threw it out at month four. Now I sort by certification first.
themes.speaker: Sophie, architect, public-sector work

example.name: Why first-time buyers abandon the cart at shipping
example.objective: Understand what tips buyers from "interested" to "forget it" in the last 60 seconds of checkout, so we know which friction to remove first.
example.q1_question: Tell me about the last time you put something in a cart and didn't buy it. What were you trying to do?
example.q2_question: What was the exact moment you thought "actually, no"? Walk me through it.
example.q3_question: If they'd done one thing differently, would you have bought? Which thing?

themes.title: Shipping cost surprise is the killer, not the amount
themes.finding: 14 of 25 abandoned not because shipping was high, but because it appeared only at the final step. Even €4.99 felt like a trap when revealed late.
themes.quote: It wasn't the five euros. It was that I'd spent ten minutes choosing and they'd been hiding it from me the whole time.
themes.speaker: Élise, urban professional, monthly online shopper

themes.title: Account creation = exit
themes.finding: Forced account creation at checkout closed the tab for 9 of 25 — half explicitly said "I'll come back later," and none did.
themes.quote: Why do I need an account to buy a t-shirt? I came to spend money, not to sign up for a relationship.
themes.speaker: Tom, occasional buyer

themes.title: Trust collapses without familiar payment options
themes.finding: Buyers expected Apple Pay / PayPal as escape hatches when the brand was new to them. Missing them = perceived sketchiness, not just inconvenience.
themes.quote: I'd never heard of them. If they don't take PayPal I assume my card info goes who-knows-where.
themes.speaker: Camille, first-time buyer from social ad

participant_demo.modal_title: Here's what your participants will see
participant_demo.modal_title_reveal: And here's what you'll see when they're done
participant_demo.modal_body: We'll ask you one quick question — the same way your participants will be asked theirs. About 30 seconds.
participant_demo.modal_body_reveal: Real interviews go through transcription, automatic highlighting, and tagging. Imagine seeing 30 of these analysed together.
participant_demo.question: Hi {{firstName}} — quick question: tell me about the best onboarding experience you had recently, and what made it stand out?
participant_demo.skip_to_example: Skip — just show me the example
participant_demo.reveal_cta: Got it — let's draft my study →
participant_demo.reveal_caption: Real studies surface dozens of these — the codes group similar moments across participants automatically.
participant_demo.error_mic_denied: Microphone access was denied. You can still see the example below.
participant_demo.error_generic: Couldn't transcribe — try again or skip to the example.
participant_demo.canned_transcript: What stood out was that they literally walked me through setting up my first project in under two minutes. I felt like I knew what I was doing right away, not like I was being tested on whether I could figure it out.
